question.text: Will Applied Materials' Q1 FY2027 revenue guidance midpoint be at or above $11.0 billion?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves on the total revenue guidance for Applied Materials' fiscal Q1 2027 (the first quarter of fiscal year 2027) contained in Applied Materials' fourth quarter and fiscal 2026 earnings press release, scheduled for Thursday, November 12, 2026 and published at https://ir.appliedmaterials.com/news-releases (expected title: "Applied Materials Announces Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2026 Results"). The guidance midpoint is the center of the guided revenue range: the stated center figure when guidance is given in the form "Total revenue $X +/- $Y" (e.g., "$10,750 +/- $500 million" has a midpoint of $10,750 million), the arithmetic mean of the low and high ends when guidance is given as a range, and the stated figure itself when guidance is given as a single value. The question resolves YES if that midpoint is at or above $11,000 million (e.g., a midpoint of $11,000 million or $11,250 million resolves YES; $10,750 million resolves NO). If the press release contains no fiscal Q1 2027 revenue guidance, revenue guidance for that quarter given in Applied Materials' Q4 FY2026 earnings call or its prepared remarks (both posted at https://ir.appliedmaterials.com) will be used; if no such guidance is published, the question is annulled. If the Applied Materials page is unavailable, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) reporting the guidance will be used.
question.fine_print: Guidance refers to Applied Materials' own total (company-wide) revenue outlook for fiscal Q1 2027 — not segment-level guidance, not the fiscal Q4 2026 results themselves, and not third-party consensus estimates.

research:
I couldn't find anything that already settles this question. Applied Materials has not given any number for fiscal Q1 2027 revenue, and the first guidance is due in the November 12, 2026 release.

## 1. Resolution source

- 2026-08-13: The latest official guidance covers fiscal Q4 2026 only: revenue of $10,250M ± $500M and non-GAAP EPS of $4.02 ± $0.20. A secondary source puts the gross margin guide at about 50.4%, operating expenses at about $1.58B and the tax rate at about 11%. [Hudson Labs](https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/applied-materials-q4-2026-earnings-preview-amat-results-preview)
- The results release and the Q1 FY2027 guide are due on 2026-11-12, after the market closes. [Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/expect-applied-materials-next-quarterly-174405444.html)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened yet that settles the question.
- 2026-08-13 (Q3 call), CFO Brice Hill: "We do expect sequential growth, in our Q1, the calendar Q4, but not guiding that at this point." [Investing.com transcript](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-applied-materials-beats-q3-2026-estimates-shares-fall-93CH-4859444)
- On the same call, he confirmed that fiscal Q1 2027 is a 14-week quarter, meaning a "higher than average step-up in our Q1 operating expenses." On how the extra week affects revenue, he said services get close to a proportional lift (the transcript reads "irratable [sic]"), "not so much on the equipment side," because "Most of the planning is done at a quarterly basis on the equipment side." That suggests the extra week may add much less than a full week's revenue. [transcript](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-applied-materials-beats-q3-2026-estimates-shares-fall-93CH-4859444)
- Other points from that call:
  - "Other" revenue is expected to average about $400M per quarter through 2027. That is below the roughly $510M guided for fiscal Q4, a headwind of about $110M if it holds.
  - Management expects "another strong record year in 2027."
  - Cleanroom availability will limit what the industry can ship. [transcript](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-applied-materials-beats-q3-2026-estimates-shares-fall-93CH-4859444)

## 4. Base rates
- The closest precedent is the last 14-week Q1. Fiscal 2021 appears to have been a 53-week year, with the extra week in Q1 ending Jan 31, 2021; that is my inference from the fiscal calendar, not confirmed by a source.
  - Q4 FY2020 actual revenue was $4.69B. The Q1 FY2021 guide was $4.95B ± $200M, about 5.5% above Q4 actual.
  - Consensus had been $4.52B, so the guide came in about 9.5% above it. [Bloomberg/BQ](https://www.bloombergquint.com/business/applied-materials-gives-sales-forecast-that-tops-estimates), [SEC 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/6951/000000695120000041/exhibit991q42020earnin.htm)
  - Actual Q1 FY2021 revenue was $5.16B. [AMAT](https://ir.appliedmaterials.com/news-releases/news-release-details/applied-materials-announces-first-quarter-2021-results)
- Recent guide-to-guide steps:
  - Q3 FY26 guide: $8.95B. Q4 FY26 guide: $10.25B (+14.5%).
  - The Q3 actual of $9.115B beat the guide by about $165M (+1.8%).
- What reaching $11.0B would take: about 7.3% above the Q4 guide midpoint. If Q4 actual comes in near $10.4-10.5B (a typical beat), the guide would need about 5-6% sequential growth, which is similar to the FY2021 precedent.
- Consensus for the January quarter:

  - Zacks: $10.74B (high $11.20B), per the question background.
- AMAT's guide ranges have recently been ±$500M wide, and midpoints typically land on $50M or $250M increments.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on AMAT's revenue guidance.
- The Kalshi market on words said during AMAT's earnings call (Nov 12) is about mentions, not revenue, so it doesn't apply directly. Prices: "EPIC Center" 0.90, "Agent/Agentic" 0.79, "Hybrid Bonding" 0.77, "Chiplet" 0.73. The other markets supplied (Tesla, Meta, Zscaler and others) are unrelated.
- Expert proxy: sell-side consensus of $10.74B sits below the $11.0B threshold. The high estimates of $11.20-11.41B are above it.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution

- Hyperscaler capex updates and China export-control news. China was 28% of Q3 revenue. [Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/expect-applied-materials-next-quarterly-174405444.html)

- **Trend:** Each guide midpoint has been above the prior quarter's actual. The Q2 guide was 9% above Q1 actual, Q3 was 13% above Q2 actual, and Q4 was 12% above Q3 actual. Actuals beat the midpoint by about $160M to $260M.
- **Arithmetic for the threshold:**
  - If Q4 lands around $10.4B, an $11.0B guide needs about 5.8% sequential growth. A flat weekly run-rate over 14 weeks would give about 7.7%.
  - If Q4 lands at $10.25B, $11.0B needs about 7.3%.
  - Guidance is usually set in $50M steps with +/- $500M ranges.
- **Earlier pattern (from memory, unverified):** January-quarter guides have often been near flat to the prior quarter. In 2025, the Q1 FY26 guide of about $6.85B compared with a Q4 FY25 guide of about $6.7B.

- Things to watch in the release:

  - How management treats the 14th week.
  - Effects of China export controls.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) The outcome is known on 2026-11-12, about 10 days from now, when Applied Materials publishes its Q4 FY2026 release after the close. For Yes, the fiscal Q1 2027 total revenue guidance midpoint must be at least $11,000M. That is about 7.3% above the Q4 guide midpoint of $10.25B and about 2.4% above the $10.74B consensus.

(b) No Q1 guide exists yet. The status quo anchor is consensus at $10.74B, which is below the threshold, so the status quo leans No.

(c) Base rate: AMAT's next-quarter guide midpoints usually land within about ±3% of consensus. Being 2.4% or more above consensus happens maybe 25-35% of the time in strong up-cycles. The FY2021 14-week Q1 precedent was a guide about 9.5% above consensus, but that came in a sharp upturn when consensus lagged. So my base rate is about 30%.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- The 14-week quarter adds revenue.
- The CFO said on 2026-08-13 that he expects sequential growth.
- Q4 actual will probably beat the guide (Q3 beat by $165M), which raises the base for Q1.
- Strong AI and memory demand: SK Hynix said on 2026-10-28 that the memory shortage could last into 2030.
- The high analyst estimates are $11.2-11.4B.

Evidence for No:
- The CFO said the extra week mostly lifts services, "not so much on the equipment side."
- "Other" revenue falls to about $400M from about $510M, a headwind of roughly $110M.
- Lam guided its December quarter up only about 5% on 2026-10-21 and cited cleanroom and parts constraints. AMAT also flagged cleanroom limits.
- Consensus of $10.74B already reflects the CFO's comments.

Segment arithmetic for the No case:
- Services: about $1.98B with the extra week.
- Other: $0.40B.
- Total: reaching $11.0B needs Semiconductor Systems at about $8.6B, roughly 9% above $7.9B. That is a bigger step than Lam's 5%.

(e) No scenario: Q4 comes in at $10.4B. Applied guides Q1 to $10.75B ± $500M, citing supply constraints and a lower Other line.

Yes scenario: Q4 comes in at $10.6B on a strong beat. Management books strong memory and advanced-packaging shipments and guides to $11.0-11.25B.

(f) I start from 30%. Peer supply constraints and the segment arithmetic pull slightly down. A likely Q4 beat and the 14-week quarter pull slightly up. The two roughly offset, so I land around 30%.

Probability: 30%

(a) Time left and the condition for Yes: about 10 days remain. Applied Materials reports on 2026-11-12 after the close. The question resolves Yes only if the fiscal Q1 2027 total revenue guidance midpoint in that release is at or above $11,000M.

(b) Status quo: no fiscal Q1 2027 guide exists yet. The best status-quo anchor is sell-side consensus of about $10.74B for the January quarter (Zacks and Yahoo). That is below the threshold, so the status quo leans No.

(c) Base rate:
- Applied's guide midpoints usually land within a few percent of consensus. They exceed consensus by 2.4% or more (what $11.0B requires) perhaps 30-35% of the time in strong upcycles.
- The only 14-week Q1 precedent, fiscal 2021, guided 9.5% above consensus. That is one data point from a different era.
- Base rate: about 33%.

(d) Strongest evidence:

For Yes:
- The fiscal Q4 guide (2026-08-13) was a 14.5% sequential step-up, a sign of an aggressive management stance.
- On the same call, the CFO explicitly said he expects sequential growth in fiscal Q1.
- Fiscal Q1 2027 is a 14-week quarter.
- AI and memory demand is strong: SK Hynix said on 2026-10-28 that the memory shortage could last into 2030.
- Fiscal 2027 consensus of about $45.6-46.4B implies average quarters above $11.4B.
- A typical Q4 beat (actual around $10.45B) would mean only about 5% sequential growth is needed to reach $11.0B.

For No:
- The CFO said on 2026-08-13 that the extra week mostly lifts services, "not so much on the equipment side."
- "Other" revenue is expected to fall to about $400M per quarter, a roughly $110M headwind against the fiscal Q4 guide of about $510M. This roughly cancels the services extra-week benefit.
- Lam guided only about 5% sequential growth on 2026-10-21, citing cleanroom and parts constraints, and Applied also flagged cleanroom limits.
- Consensus of $10.74B sits below the threshold.

(e) Scenarios:
- No: fiscal Q4 comes in at $10.4B, and management guides $10.75B ± $0.5B, citing supply constraints and lower Other revenue, with equipment roughly flat.
- Yes: fiscal Q4 comes in at $10.5B, the memory and advanced-packaging ramp accelerates, and management guides $11.0-11.25B ± $0.5B to reassure a market that has sold the stock down.

(f) Adjustment: I start at about 33%. I move up modestly because management showed a willingness to guide big step-ups last quarter, and fiscal 2027 consensus implies a rising quarterly run-rate. I hold back because the supply constraints, the Other-revenue headwind, the CFO's limited extra-week benefit for equipment and Lam's modest guide all point to a midpoint around $10.75-10.85B. The net result is about 37%.

Probability: 37%

**(a) Timing and what Yes requires.** The outcome is known about 10 days from now, after the market closes on November 12, 2026. Yes requires the Q4 FY2026 release to guide fiscal Q1 2027 total revenue to a midpoint of at least $11,000M. That is about 7.3% above the Q4 guide midpoint of $10.25B, or roughly 5% above a typical-beat Q4 actual of about $10.45B.

**(b) Status quo.** No guidance exists yet. Simply extending current expectations points to consensus of about $10.74B, which is below the threshold, so the status quo leans No.

**(c) Base rate.** For AMAT guidance midpoints landing above the January-quarter consensus by 2.5% or more, my rough estimate is 35-40%. In strong upcycles, AMAT has often guided above consensus:
- Q1 FY2021, the last 14-week quarter, was guided about 9.5% above consensus.
- The Q4 FY2026 guide was a large step-up of 14.5% guide-to-guide.
- In flatter or supply-constrained periods, guides land near consensus.

**(d) Strongest evidence.**
